author: jpjanet <jpjanet@mit.edu>
message: Revised the way in which SMILES connection information is parsed by changing inparse.py and structgen.py. In addition to being backwards compatible with existing syntax, any combination of SMILES and denticity is now supported using brackets to group smicats for each SMILES given, e.g. -lig SMI1 SMI2 -smicat [1],[3 6]. This is also now robust to mixed database/SMILES ligand order which was not possible before. In addition, the numbering systems for multiple SMILES ligands per molecule and per list has been revised to give each smiles ligand a unique number in the order it occurs. Also cleaned up old ANN files no longer in use.

author: naveenarun <notatroll.troll@gmail.com>
message:
Merge branch 'debug_mad_reentry'

This branch fixes cases where iodine molecules are considered bonded together. The new cutoff is 3.0 A for I-I bonds and 0.95*(sum of covalent radii) for I-(non I) bonds. To activate this fix, use mymol.createMolecularGraph(atom_specific_cutoffs=True) as soon as coordinates are loaded into a mol3D object.

Additionally, molecular graphs are now copied over by mol3D.copymol3D().

message:
Improved Tests

Now tests check detailed features of the geometry instead of the overal geometry:
(1) Number of atoms
(2) Metal-Ligand bondlength:
     Is the difference between the output vs reference < threshMLBL
(3) Ligand geometry. Including:
     (a) Detect  number of ligand molecules.
     (b)the number of atoms of each ligand molecule
      (c) for each ligand molecule, does the geometry match the reference: RMSD < threshLG
(4)Overall geometry:
    Is RMSD < threshOG (Usually set to large number of allow the case of ligand rotation. etc)

message:
Added the script to automatically generate test scripts for input file and reference files dumped into the inputs/ refs/ folders

After adding new input files and reference result files in the folders: tests/inputs, test/refs, we can add the corresponding python test scripts by running generateTest.py. The script will look at the inputs/ and figure out what test cases are expected to run, then look at what test scripts (test_XX.py) already exist. Then it will generate the python scripts for pytest for each new test case, given that the reference results are available. If the reference results are missing, it will complain and remind the user to provide theses files.

The way files are accessed has been cleaned up, all connections between the package and files, either in site-packages or in the new folder, should go through routines in Scripts/io.py. There may be other places where the old IO is called, these should be moved to io.py routines if they are found so any further changes are much easier. Additionally, fixed multiple bugs in the binding molecule routines, which was preventing using a SMILES string for the binding species, and added a redraw function to update the GUI when new ligands/cores/binding species are added.

message:
Overall, 1) redeigned the substrate recognition routine such that any two-body bond formation in a n-bond forming TS is performed with a [M]-sub distance as the multiplication of the sum of the atomic radii and a shrinkage ratio (formal shortness ratio), obtained by analyzing the properties of the bond forming atoms, e.g. atom symbol and hybridization and 2) allowed the recognition of C=C functional groups in a substrate to generate all epoxidation TS structures.
for mol3D.py, added getC2Cs() method to retrieve a list of C=C indices.
for the Data folder, added dictionary of FSRs
for graph_analyze.py, removed "trunc_mol.writexyz('trunc.xyz')"
for generetor.py, added args.tsgen = True when args.cdxml = True.
for inparse.py, modified the way subocc is counted when the substrate is being attached to the metal core.
for qcgen.py, protected os.remove(xxx) by try..except in multitcgen()
for structgen.py, modified many places to accomodate for bond-forming atoms recognition and all expoxidation TS generation.
for Substrates_old folder, removed it.
